title: The K-drama trope happening to you right now
dek: No dramatic reveal yet. Probably. Twelve questions about your actual week and the plot device it is quietly turning into.

questions.prompt: Your week already has a plot. It opens with:

options.label: A deal you made that's now a daily commitment
Someone from years ago reappearing
A detail everyone remembers differently
A family thing with money attached
You're being noble about something nobody asked for
You're clearly not the first choice here
It's raining and nobody brought an umbrella
You can feel a time skip coming

questions.prompt: The line you'd get in the trailer:

options.label: "It was supposed to be pretend."
"You don't remember me, do you?"
"I'm fine. Really."
"I was always standing right there."

questions.prompt: The obstacle nobody will just discuss:

options.label: You can't fully account for last Tuesday
A parent controls something you'd rather they didn't
One umbrella, two people, terrible logistics
An edit that will take three years

questions.prompt: Your behaviour that a viewer would shout at:

options.label: Following a rule you invented
Trusting a memory that keeps changing shape
A sacrifice nobody will ever know about
A small kindness with a full soundtrack
You and someone else having the same origin story
A family judging you from a very nice house
Being the reliable one, a scene behind
Knowing this chapter will end abruptly

questions.prompt: The scene that will be clipped forever:

options.label: You pretending this is casual
Someone's mother having opinions
A sentence you almost finish
Standing in the rain, obviously
A friendship that got complicated
You lost the plot, then came back to it
You protect someone from a truth
A jump cut to a much better apartment
Someone you've known since you were seven
Someone new and slightly inappropriate

questions.prompt: The plot device you'd actually choose:

options.label: One honest conversation
A dramatic exit and a reunion in five years

questions.prompt: I've retold something so many times that I now believe the new version.
I'd rather be the one who sacrifices than the one who asks.

results.name: The Contract Marriage
results.blurb: You agreed to something practical and now you're rearranging your week around it. The rules were supposed to keep this simple; instead you know their coffee order and their sister's name. Everyone can see it. You're still calling it an arrangement.
results.watchOut: Renegotiate the rules out loud. Pretending it's casual is its own drama.

results.name: The Childhood Connection
results.blurb: There's a person in your life who knew you before you were any good at being yourself. You keep finding each other at odd intervals and calling it a coincidence. It's not history holding you together — it's that you're both still the same underneath.
strengths: Good at picking up where you left off
results.watchOut: Familiar isn't automatically right. Ask what you want now, not then.

results.name: The Memory Loss Episode
results.blurb: Your account of the last few months has holes in it, and the holes are doing a lot of work. You're not lying, exactly. You've just edited so many times that the clean version feels like the true one, which is a very convenient kind of forgetting.
results.watchOut: Write the awkward version down before it disappears. The holes cost something.

results.name: The Chaebol Problem
results.blurb: Everything in your week comes with an unspoken hierarchy attached. Someone's approval matters more than it should, and you're either fighting it loudly or quietly arranging your life around it. Both of you think you're being reasonable.
results.watchOut: Not every relationship is a negotiation with a board. Let one thing be easy.

results.name: The Noble Idiocy
results.blurb: You've decided to protect someone by removing yourself from the situation, and you've told nobody why. It's very romantic in a montage. In real life it's a person standing in a doorway with no explanation and a lot of feelings.
results.watchOut: Deciding for someone isn't kindness. Give them the information and a choice.

results.name: Second Lead Syndrome
results.blurb: You do everything right, you're always there, and the story keeps looking just past you. The maddening part is that you'd be good at this. You're not bitter — you're patient in a way that the plot is currently wasting.
results.watchOut: Waiting to be chosen isn't a personality. Say the line and risk the answer.

results.name: The Umbrella Scene
results.blurb: There's a small, quiet moment this week that meant more than the big dramatic ones. You were kind at exactly the right time and then walked home slightly damp and oddly hopeful. Nobody will put it in a trailer. It's still the best scene.
results.watchOut: Atmosphere isn't communication. Say the thing in a dry room too.

results.name: The Time Skip
results.blurb: You can feel a chapter ending without knowing what the next one is. You're already imagining the reunion, the new hair, the better apartment. The trouble is you're staging the future instead of living the last few weeks of this.
results.watchOut: The montage skips the part where you have the conversation. Do it now.
